liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Opener runs about thirteen minutes, with wah-wah guitar from Jerry midway, a quieter spectral ending, and vocal reprise at 11:23; Reviewer rates a Shakedown opener plus a Terrapin as a five-star combination [14][21]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Victim a nice version [10]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Deal as ripping [10]
- **Standing On The Moon** (1 review): Reviewer lists Standing On The Moon among the fantastic performances, along with We Can Run and Throwing Stones [12]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Crazy Fingers, Playin', Terrapin sequence in the second set sick [13]
- **We Can Run** (1 review): Reviewer says this is a great version, with Brent sounding younger than usual [16]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Crazy Fingers into Playin' into Terrapin made the second set for the reviewer [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-04-11 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t02 Shakedown Street**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t03 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t04 Friend Of The Devil**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t05 Victim Or The Crime**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t06 Built To Last**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t07 We Can Run**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-11 t08 Memphis Blues Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-11.141850.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 171 min [1]
- **gd1989-04-11.148145.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 168 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd89-04-11.sbd.miller.15109.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 168 min; rated 3.44/5 by 18 [3]. Said about its sound: Heard through earbuds only, the soundboard sounds very good with good levels; Reviewer finds vocals right on but instruments perhaps a little weak in the recording; Reviewer calls it a good recording [10][12][17]
- **gd1989-04-11.156413.OTS-Schoeps-PCM-Master-Mattes-Anon-Noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 171 min [5]. Said about its sound: This transfer lacks the dropouts present in the earlier transfer [5]
- **gd1989-04-11.nak100.holtz.LMPP.94240.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [8]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is live but clear; short patches; the soundboard serves only as a patch source; Audience recording is excellent, patches included [19][21]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, 18, had balcony seats behind a speaker stack; an usher moved them to front-row mezzanine, center stage [11]
- The show opened a three-night stand at the Horizon, in Chicago's northwest suburbs, after roughly 80 seconds of tuning [14]
- Weather outside was cold and cloudy, with little lot scene, late in the tour [17]
- Reviewer felt Bob seemed under the weather, less wild than usual, while Brent's singing was stellar [21]
- Reviewer would have preferred an encore other than U.S. Blues [16]
- This is the first and only audience recording of this show [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-11.141850.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck, Sony ESX-HiFi/L750 tape); Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics, ortf (OTS) [1]. Also: An AKG C451E/CK1 source supplies several short patches, including one in Samson & Delilah [1]
- **gd1989-04-11.148145.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [2]
- **gd89-04-11.sbd.miller.15109.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> Dat -> Samplitude -> Cool Edit Pro -> SHN via Charlie Miller [3]
- **gd1989-04-11.156413.OTS-Schoeps-PCM-Master-Mattes-Anon-Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Master Audience PCM recording by Ted Mattes; transferred by Transfer by Anon Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel December 01, 2021; source: (OTS) Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics (ORTF) > Oade capacitor supply > Monster Cable ProLink > Sony pcm-f1 > Sony sl-2000 > PCM (Master) [5]. Also: Same Schoeps PCM Mattes source as shnid 141850, freshly transferred by Anon with different mastering [5]
- **gd1989-04-11.nak100.holtz.LMPP.94240.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz; transferred by Brian Green and Evan K.; source: OTS > Nakamichi CM-100's with CP-4 shotgun caps > Sony D-5 [8]. Also: Nakamichi 100 audience recording had dropouts from a faulty cable; patches came from soundboard shnid 15109 [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1989-04-11 Rosemont Horizon, Rosemont, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-04-11-rosemont-horizon-rosemont-il-usa/) [23]

facts.lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
